title: Circular Buffer
statement: Implement an 8-entry circular buffer with a write pointer and a read pointer. Writes should wrap back to the first entry after the last, and reads should return the oldest stored value. The buffer should include full and empty flags.
module_signature: module circular_buffer(input clk, input rst, input push, input pop, input [7:0] din, output reg [7:0] dout, output reg full, output reg empty);
behavior: push writes data when full is 0.
pop reads data when empty is 0.
full and empty indicate buffer status.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use built-in queue primitives.
example:
push pop | full empty dout
1 0 | 0 0 xx
0 1 | 0 0 stored
hint: Maintain separate counters for entries and wrap pointer values.
